title: Air Station Elizabeth City C-130J Hercules crew warns boaters from N.C. to N.J. of impending winter storm
description: ELIZABETH CITY, N.C. - A C-130J Hercules airplane crew from Coast Guard Air Station Elizabeth City conducts an offshore overflight pattern from the southern border of North Carolina to New Jersey warning all boaters of forecasts of heavy weather conditions for the weekend Friday, Dec. 18, 2009. Overflights such as this provide warnings to boaters who may be out of range of shore-based radio messages. (Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Mark Jones)

transcript.text: Security Security Security Hello, stations. This is the United States Coast Guard, aircraft.
It is 45 knots, so less than 150 feet in length. Please contact me on channel 22 Alpha.
U.S. Coast Guard aircraft standing by, channel 1-6.
It is a coastal and offshore area over the next 48 hours. Heavy winds, rain, snow, and severe coastal flooding is expected to accompany the storm.
Mariners are encouraged to make preparations for heavy weather and smaller vessels are encouraged to return to a safe port.
All vessels should keep the rest of the weather patterns by monitoring the National Weather Service broadcast.
There is an intense scale warning and effect through Saturday evening.
For tonight, expect 15-20 knot winds increasing the 30-35 knots with gusts up to 40 and seas building technique to 10 feet.
On Saturday, expect Northeast winds 30-35 knots becoming northwest in the afternoon.
Winds could gust as high as 42 knots, seas 10-12 feet.
Any vessel less than 150 feet in length, expect me to remain in the area through tomorrow.
Please contact the United States Coast Guard on this channel. This is U.S. Coast Guard aircraft monitoring channel 1-6.
